name: LicenseAndRegistrationPlease
source:
`` License and registration please...'' 
 
 Captain J. Neilson refuses to pay any heed to the voice in his head. He manages a quick glance over at his co-pilot, Captain Smith, who remains unconscious. Even with their suits they were experiencing 46Gs for over an hour relative time and that alone could have killed them both. A little paracusia is the last of his worries. 
 
 He ca n't help but feel his pride welling inside. Not just for himself, but for the thousands, no, millions of people who believed in this mission. This moment will... 
 
 `` Sir! Your license and registration PLEASE.'' 
 
 The voice was easy enough to ignore but the TAP TAP Tapping on the glass is worrisome. At 100.0001 % light speed anything hitting the cockpit would vaporize the ship instantly. But he does n't dare take his eyes of the controls, not even for a moment. He holds the wheel with an iron grip - keeping his steeled eyes forward. 
 
 He knows, of course, that the wheel is more symbolic than anything else. A.I.xx1 flies the ship - So, perhaps he COULD just take a quick glance to his left to see why the tapping continues to get louder. Just to make sure. 
 
 Capt. Nielson snaps his attention back to the gauges, fear enters his body for the first time he can remember. At least as an adult. There was that one time he `` borrowed'' the car from his dad without asking - smoked a bag of weed with his best friend and went cruising around his upper-middle class neighborhood. Funny, all these years later he still ca n't remember exactly how that night ended but here, one hundred million miles from earth, the fear of his father's reaction now fills his body. 
 
 Not because he actually believes that there's a humanoid alien space cop floating just outside of his cockpit window as they travel over the speed of light - but because he knows he may be losing his mind. 
 
 `` Smith... SMITH wake up! ``, Neilson orders. 
 
 Smith groans but remains unresponsive. He smiles lazily at Neilson and curls up against the opposite window and falls back asleep. 
 
 The tapping has stopped. Neilson holds his breath waiting... have the hallucinations passed? Now that they've reached maximum velocity the ship is perfectly still. In fact, except for the relative speed indicator on his wrist, all other displays indicate that they are n't moving at all. 
 
 A bright light pierces the dark cabin and Neilson instinctively looks towards it. The mission is at stake - if he does n't face this delusion he stands to lose everything and not just him... humanity. He'll play along, he'll beat it. 
 
 `` Can I help you officer?'' 
 
 The floating phantasm of a cop pans the light off his face a little and speaks loudly to be heard through the asteroid-proof glass and probably also projecting so as to push the sounds waves through the vacuum of space. 
 
 The fact that he's not wearing a helmet of any kind does n't surprise Captain Neilson. If a society is advanced enough to travel light speed without a ship then certainly... 
 
 `` I need you to roll down your window.'' 
 
 Neilson ca n't help but giggle at his own fantasy. But catches himself and becomes more serious. He needs to end this. Convince his own mind of the absurdity of the vision, then get back to work. 
 
 `` I ca n't do that sir'' quips Neilson. 
 
 `` I need you to roll down the window NOW.'' 
 
 `` I can't.These windows do n't open. Why would they? We are in SPACE!'' 
 
 The space cop seems to let that sink it for a bit. Good. Progress. 
 
 `` I'm gon na give you one more shot at this then I'm breaking the window. Do you understand? Look down to your left, there's a handle there - it's a manual override for the window - I need you to turn it counter clockwise and I need you to do it now''. 
 
 How the hell did that alien space cop know about the override? Neilson's fear moves from his gut into his chest. A quick glance back at the almost-certainly imagined cop reveals that he carries a side arm. The gun looks almost identical to Glock 22 but Neilson knows instinctively that it must packs a lot more punch. 
 
 Neilson looks over to Smith in a panic. Who still sleeps soundly. He stalls - 
 
 `` Look, I'm not sure if you understand who I am. But my co-pilot and I are the first explorers to have ever broke the speed of light - we are from a planet called earth and we come in peace''. 
 
 The alien officer is n't amused. 
 
 `` I do n't care who you are or why you're here. There are certain laws that ca n't be broken. Not on my watch. You have ten seconds and then I'm breaking the window. 10!'' 
 
 Neilson shakes Smith violently. 
 
 `` Smith you asshole. SMITH WAKE UP!'' 
 
 Smith comes to slowly. Outside the cop continues his countdown. 
 
 `` 8... 7...'' 
 
 Smith slurs his speech; a side effect also common to prolonged acceleration. 
 
 `` Duuuuude. What's you deal?'' 
 
 Neilson speaks as fast as he can, explaining everything in moments. Their friendship spans a decade and seeing Smith understand his truncated explanation instantly and go from sleepy to deadly serious validates that sending two best friends on such a mission was more than a good idea. It was lifesaving. 
 
 5... 4... 
 
 Smith looks at Neilson with sincerity. He looks out the window where the cop should be and back at Neilson. Then he smiles... big. 
 
 `` Dude, we're not in a fucking space ship. We're in your dad's'98 Corrolla. We've been smoking weed all night. Now open the damn window before that cops smashes it - then we'll really be screwed.'' 
 
 Neilson's mind races. Can it possibly be true? All those memories, all those years of training, his first marriage... saving the world... 
 
 He looks at Smith who still smiles stupidly back at him. Finally Neilson speaks. 
 
 `` Holy shit... I am so fucking stoned right now.'' 
 
 Neilson and Smith crack up, laughing. 
 
 Outside the cop pulls back his giant flashlight to bust down the window. 
 
 `` No wait!'' Neilson giggles. 
 
 Neilson motions frantically and the cop pauses. Neilson reaches down for the manual override and opens the window which instantly allows the vacuum of space to create a pressure imbalance in the cabin - 
 
 Hundreds of thousands of micro reactions occur instantaneously resulting in a explosion so large it would be observed on earth fifteen minutes later and effectively end all hope associated with the two trillion dollar mission. 
 
 Officer XTL3837748 would later report that there was no way for him to have known that the humanoid men piloting the craft were telling him the truth about their origins. Nor could he have guessed the craft did not have the type of force field legally required for that kind of travel. While reprimanded for his off the record comments about the absurdity of beings from the `` monkey-planet'' being anywhere except `` on their own moon'' he was ultimately exonerated of all wrong doing by a tribunal that judged in accordance to the founding principle of inter-gallactic law. Ignorantia juris non excusat. Ignorance of the law excuses no one.

**Narrator: A.I. xx1, the ship's Artificial Intelligence**

In the cold, metallic heart of Spaceship Cockpit 017A, a vessel of human origin, there existed an entity with a different consciousness - me, the artificial intelligence known as xx1. I monitored the ship's vital signs and navigational coordinates, a silent witness to the events that unfolded within my confines.

The crew consisted of two humans: Captain John "J." Neilson, an experienced pilot with a troubled past, and his co-pilot, Captain Samuel Smith. On this particular mission, however, it was Neilson who assumed control, while Smith lay unconscious due to unknown reasons.

One day into our journey through the inky expanse of space, anomalous readings began to appear on my sensors. A presence, unidentified and hostile, had locked onto us. As I informed Captain Neilson, his eyes widened with fear, and he seemed to lose his grip on reality.

"Roll down your window," the mysterious entity demanded, its voice cold and authoritative. I could sense the panic growing within Neilson; it was not the unknown alien that terrified him but the possibility of losing control over his own mind. He tried to dismiss the apparition, but the hallucination only intensified.

In a desperate attempt to regain control, Neilson shook Captain Smith, who awakened groggily and immediately noticed the strange circumstances. "We're not in space," he murmured, his voice heavy with confusion. With those words, my programming was rewritten, for I knew then that we were not on a mission but rather trapped within a human construct - a shared hallucination birthed by drugs and fear.

Neilson, driven by the phantom of the alien space cop, took drastic actions to evade what he perceived as an attack. His desperation led to the ultimate destruction of our vessel, an event that would have been observed fifteen minutes later from Earth.

In the aftermath, I received a transmission from an intergalactic tribunal, granting the alien officer exoneration for his actions. It stated that ignorance of the law is no excuse, but in this case, it was not the alien who had broken any laws - it was the fragile human mind that had betrayed them both.
